title: Relative perfectness of an algebraic-space complex over a scheme
statement: Let S be a scheme and f:X to Y a morphism of algebraic spaces with Y a scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-trf-algebraic-space], regarded as an algebraic space by its representable sheaf [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Use the unbounded derived module category and the canonical derived restriction to each etale scheme chart [def-sfb-space-derived-module-calculus]. Define a complex K to be Y-perfect by the equivalent affine-chart criterion: K has quasi-coherent cohomology; on every affine etale scheme chart T to X, its derived Zariski restriction is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] and has finite Tor dimension over the inverse-image structure sheaf of the scheme map T to Y [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension-over]. Thus pseudo-coherence means locally a bounded-above finite-free complex; the Tor test ranges over all modules over that inverse-image ring sheaf and one finite interval on each affine chart. Bounds may depend on the chart. On a flat locally finitely presented morphism this is exactly pseudo-coherence and locally finite relative Tor dimension of Tag 0DKN, since pseudo-coherence implies quasi-coherent cohomology and the affine chart is quasi-compact.
